_meta.title: Gaiada permission groups — the authoring layer (IAM-01b-3)
_meta.status: PROTOTYPED — 2026-08-10. Seeded from the ~40 existing platform-ui CAPABILITIES plus every grantable catalog permission they did not already reach. Pending owner/HR review before use in role authoring.
_meta.model: Two-layer (Ruling 1, option C): groups are the authoring surface; every permission remains individually assignable via an 'advanced' expansion. A group's sensitive flag is mechanical — true iff ANY member permission carries catalog sensitive:true.

groups.name: Company Overview (read-only)
groups.description: See the company profile, staff directory, user account list, org chart, and recent activity feed. View-only — no edit rights.

groups.name: Company Settings Administration
groups.description: Edit company settings and enabled modules, or delete the company (tenant) record itself.

groups.name: User Account Administration
groups.description: Create, edit, or delete/deactivate platform login accounts for people in this company.

groups.name: Edit Organization Chart
groups.description: Change the company's org chart (who reports where) — this drives automatic role and access changes for everyone under the edited unit.

groups.name: Custom Field Definitions
groups.description: Create, edit, or remove the custom fields available on projects, tasks, and other records.

groups.name: View Compliance Gates
groups.description: See the legal/compliance gates set for this company.

groups.name: Flip Compliance Gates
groups.description: Turn a legal/compliance gate for this company on or off — controls whether regulated features may run.

groups.name: Everyday Collaboration
groups.description: Comment on work, upload and manage your own files, receive notifications, and submit your own daily check-in. The baseline every staff member needs.

groups.name: Acknowledge Own Appraisal
groups.description: Acknowledge your own finalized performance appraisal. Kept separate from Everyday Collaboration because it touches HR performance data.

groups.name: Client Records
groups.description: Create, view, and edit client records.

groups.name: Delete Client Records
groups.description: Permanently delete a client record. Kept separate from everyday client management — deletion is a bigger step than editing.

groups.name: View Client Portal Contacts
groups.description: See the external contacts who have client-portal access.

groups.name: Manage Client Portal Contacts
groups.description: Create, edit, or revoke an external client contact's portal access — controls who outside the company can log in.

groups.name: Draft Client Contracts
groups.description: Create, view, and edit client contracts before they go out for signature.

groups.name: Send Contracts for Signature
groups.description: Send a client contract out for signature — the step that puts a commercial commitment in front of the client. Kept separate from drafting: see the dangerous-combination register.

groups.name: Delete Client Contracts
groups.description: Permanently delete a client contract record.

groups.name: Client Deliverables
groups.description: Create, view, edit, and delete the deliverables tracked against a client.

groups.name: View Invoices
groups.description: See client invoices.

groups.name: Manage Invoices
groups.description: Create, edit, or delete client invoices, including changing an invoice's status.

groups.name: Approve Invoices
groups.description: Approve an invoice for send/payment. Maker/checker: kept separate from Manage Invoices so an approver's authority can be granted without also granting them the ability to create/edit — and policy denies approving your own invoice regardless of this grant.

groups.name: Projects
groups.description: Create, view, edit, and delete company projects.

groups.name: Tasks
groups.description: Create, view, edit, and delete company tasks.

groups.name: Time Tracking
groups.description: Create, view, edit, and delete logged time entries.

groups.name: PM Console — Contribute
groups.description: View PM console projects and tasks, update task status/progress/dates, and pass the ball to someone else. What any team member doing project work needs.

groups.name: PM Console — Manage
groups.description: Create and delete PM console tasks, change task ownership (assign the Responsible person), and manage project settings/milestones/structure.

groups.name: Advance Delivery Pipeline Runs
groups.description: Start and advance a delivery-pipeline run, add stages, open approval gates, and view scope sign-offs. The everyday working tier for running a client engagement through its stages.

groups.name: Edit Signed Pipeline Artifacts
groups.description: Edit a delivery-pipeline stage's artifacts or status after it has already been through a stage gate. Kept separate from Sign Client Scope — see the dangerous-combination register.

groups.name: Sign Client Scope
groups.description: Record a scope sign-off with a client — the act that commits the agency to the agreed scope. Kept separate from editing signed artifacts: see the dangerous-combination register.

groups.name: Meeting Recordings
groups.description: Create, view, edit, ingest, and sync meeting recordings to the shared drive.

groups.name: Re-link Meeting Recordings
groups.description: Re-attach a recording to a different client or pipeline run. Rare and easy to misuse — can move a recording into the wrong client's context.

groups.name: File Automation Approval Requests
groups.description: File and view automation/agent write requests awaiting approval.

groups.name: File Agency Approval Requests
groups.description: File and view agency campaign/creative approval requests.

groups.name: Decide Approvals
groups.description: Approve or reject automation write requests, agency approval requests, and delivery-pipeline gates. The general approve/reject authority across the approvals inbox.

groups.name: Retry Failed Automation Actions
groups.description: Re-attempt an approved automation action that failed partway through. Narrower than Decide Approvals — deciding does not include retrying.

groups.name: Cross-Company Rollups
groups.description: Read cross-company metric rollups and trigger a recompute. The only way to see numbers spanning more than one company.

groups.name: Propose Shared Service Assignments
groups.description: Propose that one company's department provide a service to another company, and view existing assignments. Kept separate from approving — see the dangerous-combination register.

groups.name: Approve Shared Service Assignments
groups.description: Accept a proposed cross-company service assignment, which activates the cross-company access it grants. Kept separate from proposing — see the dangerous-combination register.

groups.name: Administer Service Assignments
groups.description: Suspend, resume, revoke, re-link, or reconcile an existing cross-company service assignment.

groups.name: View Integrations
groups.description: See the third-party integration connections configured for this company.

groups.name: Manage Integrations
groups.description: Create, edit, or delete third-party integration connections (OAuth/API credentials), and administer the company's connections including other people's and company-owned rows (manage, IAM-14c).

groups.name: Cross-Channel Identity Links
groups.description: View, edit, or delete the links between a WhatsApp/Telegram identity and a platform user account.

groups.name: WhatsApp Group Messaging
groups.description: Pin a message or change the subject line in a bot-managed WhatsApp group.

groups.name: WhatsApp Group Membership
groups.description: Add, remove, or promote members in a bot-managed WhatsApp group.

groups.name: Campaign Briefs
groups.description: Create, view, edit, and delete agency campaign briefs.

groups.name: Marketing Campaigns
groups.description: Create, view, edit, and delete agency marketing campaigns.

groups.name: Creative Assets
groups.description: Create, view, edit, and delete agency creative assets.

groups.name: View HR Cases & Records
groups.description: Read HR cases (onboarding, leave, loans, grievances) and HR records (contracts, documents, notes). Read-only.

groups.name: Manage HR Cases
groups.description: Create, edit, cancel, or delete HR cases such as leave, loans, onboarding, and grievances on someone else's behalf.

groups.name: Decide Leave Requests
groups.description: Approve or reject employee leave requests. Kept separate from Manage HR Cases so leave-approval authority is grantable on its own (e.g. to a department manager) without also granting general HR case management.

groups.name: Manage HR Records
groups.description: Create, edit, or delete HR records — contracts, documents, and notes on an employee's file.

groups.name: Export HR Data
groups.description: Bulk-export HR cases and records. Kept separate and requires step-up verification — bulk export is a data-exposure risk in its own right.

groups.name: View IT Devices
groups.description: See the IT device registry.

groups.name: Manage IT Devices
groups.description: Register, edit, or remove entries in the IT device registry.

groups.name: View Knowledge Sources
groups.description: Browse the sources feeding the organization-wide knowledge base (RAG).

groups.name: Review Knowledge Sources
groups.description: Approve, reject, or edit a knowledge source — controls what enters the organization-wide knowledge base.

groups.name: View Search & SEM Data
groups.description: See search-marketing properties, engagements, keywords, audits, campaigns, reports, and the provider cost ledger. Read-only.

groups.name: Draft Search & SEM Work
groups.description: Create and edit search properties, engagements, keyword sets, audits, campaign drafts and change proposals, and report drafts. Draft-only — does not touch anything live.

groups.name: Set Engagement Scope & Budget Cap
groups.description: Set a search engagement's commercial scope and provider budget cap.

groups.name: Launch Live Ad Campaigns
groups.description: Execute changes on the live ad platform — launch a campaign, apply a manual-mode change, apply negative keywords, or set the live budget. Real client ad spend. Kept separate from drafting — see the dangerous-combination register.

groups.name: Approve & Deliver SEM Reports
groups.description: Approve an engagement report and deliver it to the client. Kept separate from drafting — see the dangerous-combination register.

groups.name: Override Ad Spend Stop-Loss
groups.description: Override a provider budget stop-loss cap. Rare, high-impact, audited.

groups.name: Accept Audit-Finding Risk
groups.description: Accept risk on an open site-audit finding (with expiry or explicit indefinite) or mark it a false positive. Conceals a live, measured problem from the open-findings view — kept separate from drafting.

groups.name: Attest Property Facts
groups.description: Record an attested property fact (CMS, hosting, security posture) that a dependent audit check can resolve from on a later run. An accountability record, not a routine property edit.

groups.name: Executive Reporting
groups.description: Read company-wide report documents, view/pin/seal/amend reporting periods, and trigger a recompute of the underlying report facts. The tenant's own administrator tier.

groups.name: Team & Project Reports
groups.description: Read person-, project-, and department-grain report documents. What a department head needs to see their own unit's numbers.

groups.name: View Check-ins
groups.description: Read other people's check-in history and the compliance grid.

groups.name: Manage Check-ins
groups.description: Excuse a missed check-in. Usually granted together with View Check-ins.

groups.name: Check-in Reminders & Compliance Feed
groups.description: List pending check-in reminders and missed check-ins by org unit. Mainly consumed by the automation/reminder pipeline, not a human console.

groups.name: View Appraisals
groups.description: Read performance appraisal packs beyond your own.

groups.name: Score Appraisals
groups.description: Write and submit appraisal scores for the people you are the assigned manager for.

groups.name: Administer Appraisal Cycles
groups.description: Open, configure, and close appraisal cycles; confirm the evidence pack attached to an appraisal; and finalize an appraisal, sealing its outcome. Kept separate from scoring — see the dangerous-combination register.

groups.name: View Social Media Work
groups.description: See the content calendar, posts, the engagement inbox, client reports, the connector registry, client sign-off state, and metered spend. Read-only.

groups.name: Draft Social Content
groups.description: Create and edit posts and their per-network variants, submit them for publish approval, ask a client to sign off, and record posts published by hand. Draft-only — nothing here reaches a live account.

groups.name: Publish & Retract Social Content
groups.description: Decide that approved content goes public on a client's account, cancel a scheduled post, take a published post back down, and withdraw a pending client sign-off request. The outward-facing half of the department.

groups.name: Run the Engagement Inbox
groups.description: Reply from a client's social account, and assign, triage or escalate inbox threads.

groups.name: Approve & Deliver Social Reports
groups.description: Sign off a social-media client report and send it to the client.

groups.name: Connect Social Accounts
groups.description: Connect a client's social account to our platform app, edit connector-registry entries, and disconnect.

groups.name: Set Social Scope & Spend
groups.description: Set an engagement's tool scope and metered budget, delete an engagement, and override a metered stop-loss. This is the money and blast-radius dial for the department.

groups.name: Manage Social Platform Apps
groups.description: Our own approved developer-app fleet across the networks: registrations, app-review outcomes, and credential aliases. Global, not per-client.

groups.name: File Website Change Requests
groups.description: File and view website change requests.

groups.name: Triage Website Change Requests
groups.description: Accept, route, or reject an incoming website change request.

groups.name: Website Provisioning
groups.description: Provision a client site's real infrastructure (repo + hosting) and re-check its provisioning status.

groups.name: WebDesk Contract Snapshots
groups.description: View a client site's pinned WebDesk contract (the Contract card) and refresh it from the platform's control channel -- the one-rail mirror, WSK-19.

groups.name: Client Portal — Basic Access
groups.description: Open the client portal workspace, file a website change request, and update your own client-contact profile.

groups.name: Client Portal — Sign Documents
groups.description: Sign a contract or scope document from the client portal.

groups.name: Client Portal — Pay Invoices
groups.description: Initiate payment of an invoice from the client portal.

groups.name: Client Portal — Decide Gates
groups.description: Decide a gate that has been exposed to the client in the portal.

groups.name: Client Portal — Approve Social Posts
groups.description: Approve, or request changes to, social posts drafted for your brand before they are published.

groups.name: View Monitoring
groups.description: See monitors, their check results, incidents, uptime, scheduled maintenance windows, notification channels and status-page configuration. Read-only.

groups.name: Create & Edit Monitors
groups.description: Create monitors and edit their target, assertions, interval and severity. Creating a monitor is the standing authorization for the platform to probe that target on a schedule — and nothing more.

groups.name: Delete Monitors
groups.description: Delete monitors and their check history. Destructive and unrecoverable, so it is a separate group from ordinary editing — though not catalog-sensitive, since it destroys our own records rather than reaching outside the ERP or concealing an outage.

groups.name: Acknowledge Incidents
groups.description: Acknowledge an open monitoring incident — the accountability record that a named person has seen it. Deliberately not an edit.

groups.name: Schedule Maintenance Windows
groups.description: Schedule and cancel maintenance windows. A window suppresses BOTH notification and SLA math for its duration, so it can hide a real outage and flatter an uptime figure.

groups.name: Manage Notification Channels
groups.description: Create, edit and test notification channels and routing rules. Channels carry secret references and deliver outward; a test sends a real notification.

groups.name: Publish Client Status Pages
groups.description: Edit and publish client status pages. This is the only path that moves tenant monitoring state onto the ERP's one unauthenticated read surface.

groups.name: View HR Policies & Calendars
groups.description: Read the company's own HR rules — public-holiday calendars, leave policies and entitlements, review-cycle windows, the pay-grade structure, and the statutory parameter sets. Deliberately broad: these govern everyone, and hiding a holiday calendar from the people it applies to is a support ticket, not a security posture.

groups.name: Manage HR Policies & Calendars
groups.description: Create and amend HR configuration: holiday calendars, leave policies and their assignments, review cycles, pay grades, and statutory parameter sets. Does NOT include ratifying those parameters — that is its own group.

groups.name: Ratify Statutory Parameters
groups.description: Sign off a set of statutory payroll numbers (tax brackets, BPJS rates and caps, severance multipliers) as verified, which is what unblocks finalizing a payroll run against them. Kept separate from Manage HR Policies on purpose: the routine edit that fixes a typo in a calendar name must not also be able to declare the tax tables legally correct. Requires step-up verification.

groups.name: View Recruitment
groups.description: Read requisitions, candidates, applications, interviews and scorecards. A hiring manager or interview panelist reaches their OWN pipeline without this group, through the application's own participants.

groups.name: Manage Recruitment
groups.description: Run the hiring pipeline: create requisitions and candidates, advance applications, schedule interviews, file scorecards, and draft offers. Does not include approving a requisition or an offer, nor turning an accepted offer into an employee.

groups.name: Approve Hiring & Convert Offers
groups.description: Approve a requisition or an offer, and convert an accepted offer into an employee record. Separate from Manage Recruitment because these three commit headcount, commit money, and turn an outsider into someone the access reconciler can reach. Requires step-up verification.

groups.name: Export Candidate Data
groups.description: Bulk-export the candidate pool. Kept separate because candidates are outsiders whose data is held under consent with a retention clock, not employees under contract. Requires step-up verification.

groups.name: View Compensation & Payroll
groups.description: Read salary records, allowances, benefit enrolments, tax profiles, payroll runs, payslips and separations — for the whole company. A deliberate step above View HR Cases & Records: an HR assistant who files leave and uploads contracts should not hold this. An employee reads their OWN published payslip without any group.

groups.name: Manage Compensation & Payroll
groups.description: Set compensation, assign allowances and benefits, capture payroll inputs, create and calculate payroll runs, and draft separations. Calculating a run does not pay anybody — approving it does, and that is a separate group.

groups.name: Approve Payroll & Separations
groups.description: Approve a payroll run, a compensation change, or a separation payout, and mark a run paid. This is the action that commits money. Requires step-up verification.

groups.name: Export Payroll Register
groups.description: Export the payroll register or bank file. Requires step-up verification.

groups.name: View Chart of Accounts & Calendar
groups.description: Read the accounting vocabulary — chart of accounts, dimensions and cost centres, the fiscal period calendar, currencies and exchange rates. Carries no figures: an account code and name are not money. Needed by anyone coding an expense or a document to the right account.

groups.name: Manage Chart of Accounts & Calendar
groups.description: Own the accounting vocabulary: create, edit and delete accounts, dimensions and dimension values, cut fiscal years and periods, enter exchange rates, and set the company's functional and presentation currency. The controller/accountant tier. An account that has ever been posted to is additionally frozen in the database — it can be renamed and archived, never re-typed or re-coded.

groups.name: Lock & Close Fiscal Periods
groups.description: Run the period close: soft-lock a period to stop ordinary posting, reopen it if the close finds something, and hard-close it to assert the figures are final. Hard-closing is IRREVERSIBLE and requires step-up verification plus a named accountant's sign-off — a wrong figure in a closed period is fixed by a correcting entry in an open one, never by reopening. Deliberately separate from managing the chart of accounts: one person holding both could post an adjustment and then close the books over it.

groups.name: Govern Finance Duties & Access
groups.description: The governance tier: assign finance duties, waive a segregation-of-duties conflict under a compensating control, approve or revoke cross-company finance elevation, and read the finance access log. Held ABOVE the accounting tiers because it governs them — whoever can assign duties can assign themselves any duty. Every action requires step-up verification. Note this does NOT decide which companies an owner may see: that comes from the ownership graph.

groups.name: Browse the Learning Catalogue
groups.description: See courses, learning paths and what has been assigned. Deliberately broad — training you cannot see is a support ticket, not a security posture. Progress and scores are a SEPARATE group.

groups.name: Author Training
groups.description: Create, edit and retire courses and learning paths. A department head is scoped to their OWN department by the org chart; the LMS manager tier and company admins author company-wide. Does NOT include publishing.

groups.name: Publish Training
groups.description: Publish a course version, making it assignable and freezing the content people will be certified against. Kept separate from authoring because saving a draft and declaring it fit to certify against are different acts.

groups.name: Delete Training Content
groups.description: Hard-delete a course. Rarely correct — a course with completions against it should be RETIRED, so the certificates people hold remain readable.

groups.name: View Training Progress
groups.description: Read enrolments, progress and scores for others. A learner reads their OWN without this group; a department head sees their unit; HR sees company-wide for compliance. Includes failed attempts, which are more sensitive than passes.

groups.name: Assign Training
groups.description: Assign learning paths to people and record progress on their behalf. The mandatory general track is auto-assigned and needs no one to hold this.

groups.name: Grade Submissions
groups.description: Grade a submitted attempt for a reviewed activity — UI/UX work and management scenarios, where a rubric beats an assertion. Separate from assigning so a learner can never grade themselves.

groups.name: Waive Mandatory Training
groups.description: Excuse somebody from training they are required to complete. A compliance decision rather than an assessment one — and deliberately NOT held by department heads, who would otherwise be able to excuse their own team from the company's mandatory track.

groups.name: Export the Training Register
groups.description: Bulk-export who passed what, when, and with what score. Personal data about every employee at once; requires step-up verification.

groups.name: View & Verify the Ledger
groups.description: Read journal entries and their lines, and run the ledger integrity check (hash chain, sequence gaps, balance). Verification is deliberately wide: an integrity check that only the person who could have broken the chain may run is not an integrity check.

groups.name: Post & Reverse Journals
groups.description: Post journal entries to the book of record, and correct them by reversal — the only sanctioned correction, since a posted journal can never be edited or deleted. Reversal sits at the same tier as posting on purpose: making corrections harder than postings pushes people toward not correcting at all. Deliberately NOT granted alongside period-close rights: journal posting plus period closing is a blocking segregation-of-duties conflict.

groups.name: View Financial Statements
groups.description: Read the trial balance, general ledger, profit and loss and balance sheet for the company. Deliberately wider than reading the ledger itself: a statement is an aggregate, and someone who should see departmental cost totals does not thereby need every journal line behind them.

groups.name: Export Financial Statements
groups.description: Produce financial statements as a file that leaves the ERP — the pack a bank, auditor or board actually reads. A separate right from viewing because the artefact outlives the session and carries no access control once it exists. Requires step-up verification.

groups.name: View Receivables & Aging
groups.description: Read AR customers, invoices, receipts and the aging schedule, and run the subledger-to-ledger reconciliation check. Reconciliation is deliberately wide — a tie-out only the person who could have broken it may run is not a check.

groups.name: Run the Receivables Desk
groups.description: The AR officer's day job: maintain customers and draft invoices, issue invoices to the ledger, and record and allocate customer receipts. Does NOT include writing off a debt — that is the other half of the classic receivables fraud pair and is granted separately.

groups.name: Write Off Receivables
groups.description: Void an issued invoice or forgive a receivable — the action that makes money owed to the company disappear. Held apart from receipt posting because holding both is a blocking segregation-of-duties conflict (pocket the cash, then write off the debt). Requires step-up verification.

groups.name: View Payables & Aging
groups.description: Read AP vendors, bills, payments and the aging schedule, and run the subledger-to-ledger reconciliation check.

groups.name: Enter Vendor Bills
groups.description: Enter and edit draft vendor bills. Nothing reaches the books until a bill is approved, which is a separate right — entering and approving your own bill is a blocking segregation-of-duties conflict.

groups.name: Maintain Vendors & Bank Details
groups.description: Create and edit vendors, including the bank accounts payments are sent to. Held apart from payment release because holding both is a blocking conflict — invent a vendor, pay yourself — and because redirecting the bank details on a genuine invoice needs no fake bill at all. Requires step-up verification.

groups.name: Approve Vendor Bills
groups.description: Approve a bill so it posts to the ledger, committing the company to pay the vendor and to remit any withheld tax. Requires step-up verification.

groups.name: Release Vendor Payments
groups.description: Release payment to a vendor — the moment money irreversibly leaves the company. The narrowest grant in the finance module: not held by AP clerks who enter bills, and not by company administrators. Requires step-up verification.

groups.name: View Bank Reconciliation
groups.description: Read bank statements and match state, run the bank reconciliation, and run the period close-readiness check that aggregates every integrity test in the finance module.

groups.name: Run Bank Reconciliation
groups.description: Import bank statements and match their lines to the ledger. Held by finance staff deliberately: staff cannot release payments, so a staff member reconciling satisfies the segregation-of-duties rule that whoever moves money must not be the one declaring the bank agrees.

groups.name: View Tax Position
groups.description: Read tax codes, returns, the PPN and PPh summaries, and the e-Faktur exception lists — including input VAT the company is losing because a vendor has not issued a faktur.

groups.name: Prepare Tax Returns
groups.description: Build draft returns, import the Coretax extract, and run the reconciliation between our ledger and the tax office-s pre-populated data. Asserts nothing to anyone — filing is a separate right.

groups.name: Configure Tax Codes
groups.description: Create and amend tax codes: rates, base multipliers and effective dates. This changes the tax computed on every future document, so it sits with the controller tier and requires step-up verification.

groups.name: File Tax Returns
groups.description: Mark a return as filed with the tax office and record its reference. A statement to the state: an understated return means an assessment plus penalties, and an overstated one is money that is hard to recover. Requires step-up verification.

groups.name: View Posting Rules & Event Queue
groups.description: Read the mappings from business events to accounts, the finance event inbox, and the backlog of events that have not posted — including failures and why.

groups.name: Process Finance Events
groups.description: Run business events through their posting rules and sweep the pending queue. Applies a mapping somebody else authored and approved; every posting still passes the ledger-s own guards. This is the grant an automation or agent principal may legitimately hold.

groups.name: Author Posting Rules
groups.description: Draft and edit the mappings from business events to accounts. Drafting is ordinary work; making a rule live is a separate right, because a single activation re-points an entire event stream.

groups.name: Activate Posting Rules
groups.description: Make a posting rule live, or retire one. This decides where revenue, cost and tax appear in the financial statements for every future event of that type. Requires step-up verification.

advancedOnly.reason: IAM Phase 2 (P2-02): the action that actually confers a position's role-set to a person — advancedOnly until the dept-head access page (P2-11) lands.
IAM Phase 2 (P2-02): org-chart seat administration — advancedOnly until the positions admin UI (P2-12) curates a dedicated group.

IAM Phase 2: deciding a placement request. advancedOnly beside core.role_grant.create/.decide_override — it belongs behind the grant/position authoring surfaces with the requester-not-decider and ceiling checks in front of it, not in a friendly group picker.
IAM Phase 2 (P2-02): see core.position.create.
IAM Phase 2 (P2-02): see core.position.create.
IAM Phase 2 (P2-02): pairs with core.position.assign — same reasoning.
IAM Phase 2 (P2-02): see core.position.create.

IAM Phase 2 (P2-02): the granting authority itself — deliberately advancedOnly rather than folded into a friendly group until the position/grant authoring UI (P2-04/P2-08/P2-11) lands with its own ceiling/allow-list checks in front of it.

IAM Phase 2 (P2-08 part B): the authority to DECIDE a routed override. advancedOnly for the same reason its sibling core.role_grant.create is — it belongs behind the grant-authoring surfaces (P2-11) with the ceiling, allow-list and requester-not-decider checks in front of it, not in a friendly group picker where it reads like an ordinary approval duty.
IAM Phase 2 (P2-02): audit visibility over who holds which grants — advancedOnly alongside its sibling create/revoke actions rather than split into its own group.
IAM Phase 2 (P2-02): pairs with core.role_grant.create — same advancedOnly reasoning.
Machine/automation tracker-event ingestion (bot/agent writes). Not a duty a human role is composed for; would confuse a group picker with a technical write action.
Raw tracker event stream — a support/debugging read, not an everyday duty. (core.activity.read, the human-facing activity feed, is already in Company Overview.)

UI-01b: writing an ownership edge CONFERS SCOPE — a holding edge reaches every descendant company, so a writer can widen their own reach by inserting one row naming themselves. advancedOnly beside core.role_grant.create for the same reason: it belongs behind an authoring surface with checks in front of it, never in a group anyone can hand out.

UI-01b: the cap table. advancedOnly until the ownership admin surface (UI-01c) lands — same treatment as core.position.read. It is also not merely a finance read: finance_owner_company_ids() resolves a person's VISIBILITY from this table, so the shareholder register is an authorization fact and does not belong in a friendly group picker beside 'view the chart of accounts'.

UI-01b: pairs with finance.ownership.create — same reasoning. Note this is also how a holder is REMOVED (by end-dating), because ownership is effective-dated and there is deliberately no delete action.
IAM Phase 2 (P2-02): the HR people file — advancedOnly until the HR console's hire/transfer/terminate flows (P2-10) land with their own typed forms in front of it.
IAM Phase 2 (P2-02): see hr.employee.create.
IAM Phase 2 (P2-02): see hr.employee.create.
IAM Phase 2 (P2-02): see hr.employee.create.
IAM Phase 2 (P2-02): see it.account.provision.
IAM Phase 2 (P2-02): see it.account.provision.
IAM Phase 2 (P2-02): mints a Keycloak login — advancedOnly, same reasoning as it.account.read.
IAM Phase 2 (P2-02): the IT accounts worklist — advancedOnly until the IT accounts console (P2-13/P2-14) lands over keycloak-admin.ts.
IAM Phase 2 (P2-02): see it.account.provision.

WSK-12: the only legitimate caller is the wd-zoneb-intake automation identity (WSK-31 provisions it). Granting this to a human in a role editor would let them inject facts that look like they came from Zone B, which the signed-webhook boundary exists to prevent.
